item.title: Gemini 4 Hydrogen performance varies significantly between 'high' and 'xhigh' effort levels
item.description: Gemini 4 Hydrogen on 'high' effort level used 5,311 output tokens and cost 3.99 cents, while on 'xhigh' effort level it used 31 tokens and cost 23.61 cents. item.title: Muru: AI-assisted Rust Server for Python Web Apps by Graham Dumpleton
item.description: Graham Dumpleton, creator of mod_wsgi, has developed Muru, an AI-assisted Rust server for ASGI and WSGI Python applications, detailing its development process in a series of blog posts. Muru addresses the need for better tools to run Python web applications in both development and production environments, leveraging AI to enhance efficiency. — Upstream (Simon Willison): https://simonwillison.net/2026/Nov/21/muru/

item.title: Rapid improvement in open-weights models may slow due to distillation limits
item.description: The effective end of easy distillation from OpenAI and Anthropic models may be behind the relative slowdown in open-weights model progress. The rapid improvement in open-weights models has slowed down, possibly due to the difficulty in distilling knowledge from established models. — Upstream (Bluesky · @emollick): https://bsky.app/profile/emollick.bsky.social/post/3n2req7quy225

item.title: I was driving and wondered how many signals pass through me at any given moment. Here’s what Claude Duet created in 15 mins.

item.title: Two Mathematicians Independently Prove Riemann Hypothesis Within Hours
item.description: Within a few hours of each other, Levent Alpöge of Anthropic and Elliot Glazer independently claimed proofs of the Riemann Hypothesis, the most famous open problem in mathematics. The Riemann Hypothesis, a conjecture about the distribution of prime numbers, has been independently proven, potentially revolutionizing number theory and its applications. — Upstream (Swyx · Latent Space): https://latent.space/p/ainews-riemann-hypothesis-proved-twice-independently/

item.description: The test demonstrates the differences between Gemini 4 Carbon and Gemini 4 Neon models running at different effort levels. It highlights the variations in performance between models within the same family, aiding in understanding their capabilities. — Upstream (Bluesky · @simonwillison): https://bsky.app/profile/simonwillison.net/post/3n2nhnbueh22q

item.title: Distillation can reproduce powerful AI capabilities without the safeguards built around them
item.description: Research from OpenAI shows that distillation can reproduce powerful AI capabilities without maintaining the original model's safeguards. The issue is that distillation could lead to the loss of safety measures, which are crucial for applications like banking. — Upstream (X · @OpenAI): https://x.com/OpenAI/status/2123862344422088794

item.title: MedChemBench: New benchmark for AI reasoning in medicinal chemistry
item.description: MedChemBench is a new benchmark introduced for evaluating AI reasoning capabilities in medicinal chemistry. It aims to provide a standardized method for assessing AI's ability to reason about complex chemical structures and interactions. — Upstream (X · @OpenAI): https://x.com/OpenAI/status/2123856316187975756

item.title: Human-driven proof of Generalized Riemann Hypothesis under review
item.description: Alessandro Masullo has proposed a proof of the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis, and Brian Conrad has been reviewing it with extensive feedback. The work is entirely human-driven, with no AI involved. The team aims to refine the proof and announce it after thorough review, ensuring the highest level of accuracy and reliability. — Upstream (Simon Willison): https://simonwillison.net/2026/Nov/20/ravi-vakil/

item.title: Levent Alpöge claims Riemann Hypothesis proof with AI assistance
item.description: Levent Alpöge claims to have discovered a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis with Claude's help, extending it to the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis. They formalized the arguments without assumptions. The Riemann Hypothesis, a long-standing problem in mathematics, and its generalizations, which have implications in number theory and beyond. — Upstream (Simon Willison): https://simonwillison.net/2026/Nov/20/levent-alpoge/

item.title: Using Formal Verification to Combat Low-Quality AI Output in Banking
item.description: Formal verification systems, which use mathematical proofs and logic to verify software correctness, are being adopted by AI companies like &Truth to combat low-quality AI-generated code. The growing reliance on AI-generated code has led to concerns about low-quality output, necessitating tools that can ensure the reliability and correctness of the code. — Upstream (Swyx · Latent Space): https://latent.space/p/formal-verification/

item.title: Combatting Adversarial Distillation in AI Models
item.description: OpenAI developed a layered approach to protect AI models from adversarial distillation, a technique where bad actors can extract and use model capabilities without proper safeguards. The problem is that adversaries can use AI models' outputs to train new models with similar capabilities, potentially bypassing the original model's safety mechanisms. — Upstream (OpenAI News): https://openai.com/index/combatting-adversarial-distillation

item.title: Can AI help scientists identify promising drug candidates?
item.description: MedChemBench evaluates how well AI models interpret molecular structures, reason from experimental evidence, and select compounds in early drug discovery.
